records.issue_text: `match_count += 1; save` in BlockedEmail is a read-modify-write race; concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose increments (use increment_counter/update_all)
records.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code loads a row (`where(...).first`), then does `record.match_count += 1` and `record.save`. This is a classic read-modify-write sequence that is not atomic; concurrent signups hitting the same blocked email can overwrite each other’s increments and lose updates to `match_count` (and potentially `last_match_at`). records.issue_text: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` on the create_account_controller class prototype is shared across all controller instances (Ember prototype-array pitfall); should be initialized in `init`
records.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined as a mutable object on the class prototype via `Discourse.Controller.extend(...)`. In Ember, this means the same array instance can be shared across controller instances, so `pushObject` in the failure path can leak state between instances/usages unless it’s re-initialized per-instance (e.g., in `init`).
